Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

next year phrase

classical

Cic. Att. 5.2.1
Cic. de Or. 3.92: faciendum est ad annum
Traupman 409

ad annum

next year, a year from now

“For the coming year, a year hence” (Lewis & Short); unlike proximō annō, it cannot mean last year.

Other words

  • in proximum annum — for next year

    also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 4.15.5; Caelius in Cic. Fam. 8.9.2

    With verbs of putting off, wishing or choosing.

  • proximō annō — next year; last year

    also used · classical · Traupman 89: proximus annus, “the following year”; Plin. Ep. 10.5.1

    proximus is the nearest year either way: Pliny’s proximō annō (Ep. 10.5.1) is last year.

  • īnsequentī annō — the following year (in narrative)

    also used · classical · Liv. 3.2.1

Examples

  • Furnium nostrum quem ad annum tribūnum pl. vidēbam fore

    our friend Furnius, who I could see would be tribune next yearCic. Att. 5.2.1

  • optāmus enim tibi ōmināmurque in proximum annum cōnsulātum

    for we wish you, and foresee for you, the consulship next yearPlin. Ep. 4.15.5

See also next week, every year, last week, year.

SourcesLewis & Short: annus · Lewis & Short: proximus
